method:
Adjudication of the 10 disputes of part g-east (prims 'sukhumvit', area 'ground', box x 31-54.5 / y 5-26.2), decided from the drawing, never by majority. The 11 accepted openings are copied unchanged; nothing in the drawing contradicted them.

For each dispute I rendered the spot with render.py (grid 0.25, inserts, some with text). I queried every entity around it from prims.pkl (q.py: layer, handle, linetype, exact points). I read the context: hatches (pool water E274 vs deck E105), furniture blocks (the kitchen base counter), and linetypes (HIDDEN, CENTER2 and PHANTOM2 lines are overhead edges, grid lines or the property line, not walls). Where it bears on kind, I used the east elevation geometry (tags AW1/D1/AD1/D3 and their operation marks). Kinds follow the refined definition: window = glazing not walked through, whatever its sill; door = walked through (sliding glass doors onto a deck included); passage = walk-through gap with nothing drawn. Ends are on the host wall's centre line at the WALL-layer faces (frames included); width = |b-a|.

Completeness: a sweep (sweep.py) listed every DOOR, D-JAMB, WIN, W_Grill, A_Grill, WALL-GL, DSYM and xref-door item, every arc of radius > 0.3 m on any layer, and every door/window-like insert in the part. Each was checked against the final openings, glass walls and rejected spots. The leftovers are explained: g-west glazing and fences, wardrobe and closet bi-fold arcs, sofa curves, the driveway kerb arc, and the pedestrian gate's own leaf tip and post. Then one render of the whole part, with a marker at every final opening, was checked for unmarked swings, leaves, jamb pairs, window bands or clean gaps. Close renders of the porch, the plinth crossed by steps, the east block and the south edge were checked too. The only new opening all opinions missed in this pass is none beyond GE-20 (E only, confirmed).

Result: 20 openings (13 doors, 5 windows, 2 passages), 4 glass walls. Agreement: 11 both, 6 fixed, 3 one. Self-score with score.py: 20/20.

Note for the orchestrator: tools/score.py crashes with a TypeError whenever a matched pair differs in class and the key opening has no 'eitherKind' field. k.get('eitherKind') returns None, so c_ok = False or None = None, and n['class'] += None fails. No part key uses eitherKind, so any class mismatch will crash the gate run. Wrapping c_ok in bool() fixes it. A patched copy, used only for my checks, is out/adjudicate-g-east/score_patched.py. With it, A scores 16/20 right and B 17/20 against this key; the differences are exactly the decided items.
